description: Prepare an isolated practice setup with snapshots, test accounts and controlled targets. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 2 — Build a safe Linux and virtual lab

LEARNING OUTCOME
Prepare an isolated practice setup with snapshots, test accounts and controlled targets.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Use a virtual machine or deliberately vulnerable training app. Prefer a host-only or isolated virtual network, non-sensitive test accounts, snapshots and disposable data. Do not connect a vulnerable lab directly to a work or home network unless the exposure is intentional and controlled.

blocks.text: Commands such as `pwd`, `whoami`, `ip addr`, `ss -tulpen`, `ls -la` and `man` help inspect your own environment. Learn paths and permissions. Do not run unknown scripts with administrator privileges or paste secrets into shell history.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — Private network. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Snapshot. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Create a snapshot before experiments. Record lab version and time. If behavior is unexpected, stop and restore the snapshot instead of escalating privileges or trying the same action against a live target.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Run only in your own sandbox/VM and consult the official manual.

blocks.question: Before Lesson 2 testing, what should be confirmed?
options: A friend said it is okay
The exact target is covered by written permission
blocks.explanation: Written permission should define target and allowed methods.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: How should a finding from Lesson 2 be handled?
options: Include a real password as proof
Save minimal redacted evidence and report through the approved channel
blocks.explanation: Findings need scoped, protected and reproducible evidence.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What requires the learner to stop?
options: A lab result needs an explanation
Target is out of scope or testing may cause unexpected harm
blocks.explanation: Stop if scope or safety limits may be crossed.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?
options: Retest the same authorized condition and document the result
blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
options: Stop and ask the owner to clarify permission
blocks.explanation: Scope is a boundary; do not proceed without permission.
